findings.reason: Step 1.1 extracts convergent subsequences of boundary points from compactness. The declared suppliers establish compactness but not sequential compactness for this compact metrizable boundary, and the proof gives no finite-cover argument. Add or prove that prerequisite (for example, compact-metric sequential compactness with the metric-topology identification), or replace the sequence argument. This blocks the direct consumer lem-ip-simple-geodesic-polar-extension and its downstream consumers lem-ip-simple-geometry-global-eikonal-geometric-optics, thm-ip-wave-data-determine-light-ray-integrals, cor-ip-wave-coefficient-uniqueness-under-simple-geometry, and ex-ip-40-simple-geometry-adequate-observation-time.

The added F7 supplies compactness of the ambient tangent-space sphere and ball, but Step 1.1 also needs compactness of the boundary-tangent unit sphere for a uniform convexity bound, and Steps 1.1–2.1 extract convergent subsequences of inward directions. The dependencies do not supply the needed closed-subspace compactness and sequential-compactness results (such as cor-bolzano-weierstrass-in-rn). This leaves the uniform exit and radial-domain arguments incomplete and blocks the same downstream consumers listed for the no-return lemma.

The Cauchy–Schwarz error estimate is sound. Its wave-application paragraph does not delimit the application to beams satisfying the supplier's required temporal-endpoint condition (zero near the initial or terminal slice); extending endpoint residuals outside the measurement domain alone does not state that condition. Specify the applicable ray and extension hypotheses, including the supplier's physical-time phase normalization, and connect them to the correction claim.
